title: fix(update): restore Gateway and clear stale warnings after repair
body:
Related: #150950 #151132. Also related: #150942. Reported by @shadesurgeon.

## What Problem This Solves

Successful `openclaw update repair` could leave stale failure warnings and recovery actions visible, full repair delegated service activation to its Doctor child, and updater children omitted valid recovery guidance on ordinary maintenance refusals. An explicit finalization deadline could also exit the parent before asynchronous Gateway restoration, leaving the managed service stopped.

The original 2026.9.4 self-conflict is already fixed on main by #147720 (`fe645cd77de7`), and missing failure reasons by #147286 (`d10ef37bfd56`). Both fixes are included in the 2026.9.5 cut. This is a normal follow-up that completes the recovery UX.

## User Impact

Healthy abandoned-run recovery stays online. Full repair stops and restores its owned Gateway through the update parent; Doctor children never stop or restart it. A fatal phase deadline cancels work, fences late writes, allows bounded settlement, and records the phase/deadline warning. The parent restores and verifies the Gateway before exiting with the original failure code. A restoration failure identifies the problem and the restart command. CLI and Control UI recovery prompts clear after acknowledgement while historical failure records remain available.

Unavailable service inspection still allows state repair under its database owners without claiming service authority. Other maintenance refusals retain the independent `openclaw doctor --fix` recovery step; only the explicit self-parent activation refusal omits that guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Doctor's maintenance owner in the update parent: acquire lifecycle ownership before service stop, release database fences before fresh Doctor children, then restore and verify the owned service after convergence or failure. Inspect newer failed post-core attempts, including legacy rows with empty reasons, so an older abandoned row cannot bypass necessary finalization.

Keep acknowledgement predicates in the browser-safe record owner. Both record and legacy-expiry modules consume the type-only `update-run-recovery-state.ts` contract; the value dependency is record → legacy expiry, which owns the terminal reason. Recovery guidance follows the actual parent-activation refusal, rather than the presence of an update-parent marker.

Finalization reuses the activation deadline owner for cancellation and bounded joining. Native service custody is acquired and restored outside the canceled mutation phase; restoration revalidates the original live maintenance instance and current native service ownership. Terminal exit follows restoration instead of bypassing its `finally`.

No config options, CLI options, database schema, or dependencies change.

## Evidence

- Tooling entry fix (`63bc9ba3ac62fb118f19d2496eb02c76ccd078dc`): the deadline proof is an internal phase of the explicitly selected abandoned-update qualification. Its logic now lives in the already-registered `abandoned-update.mjs` CLI as `deadline-hook` and `deadline-verify`; the separate unregistered helper was deleted. Knip configuration and the scenario catalog are unchanged.
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` passes with **0 production and 0 full-tree unused files**. All **177 survivor plan, registry, and systemd-fixture tests** pass. Before/after executable CLI checks produced identical hook bytes and verification output, and both rejected invalid late-write evidence. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed after the move.
- Rebased onto `2d05f4c3b677105cf98c58732862713c85c08e0e`, containing #151132. The fresh-Doctor external-policy handoff, authenticated systemd template-instance resolver, refusal-only fast path/classifier/transaction, and new refusal cases were preserved byte-for-byte. Three import hunks were resolved in the repair command, its test, and the run ledger; the existing four commits were preserved, followed by the test-only assertion commit.
- The executable CLI deadline regression failed before the fix because the Gateway remained stopped. After the fix it records `stop → plugins-entered → late-write-refused → restart`, keeps config unchanged, records the warning, releases custody, and preserves exit code 1. Copied, consumed, released, and concurrently revoked maintenance handles cannot restore the service.
- The selected Doctor maintenance, health, repair/finalization, executor, external-policy, refusal-only, and systemd-template coverage passes: **430 tests across 20 files**, using one worker. Two obsolete downgrade call-shape assertions were strengthened to verify one mutation, guard presence by mode, and refusal after finalization phase closure; no production code changed for that adjustment.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check` pass. Both runtime and Madge import checks report **0 cycles**. No suppressions, baseline growth, or test weakening.
- Production review of record: committed head `91358d3a7345eddd0c63258f4028bfccc9897a66` (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1`) is **scoped-clean (0.85)**. Production code is unchanged. The tooling-only consolidation received a local Codex review: **scoped-clean (0.97)**.
- Linux packaged qualification with the published **2026.9.4** driver passed after rebasing over #151132: online abandoned-run recovery preserved the Gateway; full repair stopped and restored it under the update parent; the injected **15,000 ms plugins deadline** refused a late real config write, restored the Gateway, released custody, recorded the warning, and exited 1. All health probes passed. The systemd managed-service fixture substitutes for the container's unavailable `systemd --user`; Doctor never issued a service mutation. Provider: `blacksmith-testbox`; lease `tbx_01m2rp119n18z8rfzhetze66sb`; [qualification run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35279557379); wrapper exit **0**, command time **13m58s**; lease stopped. Qualified source: `16da82964cc0c47e9b421ced2749f0daea32b191`; later commits strengthen test assertions and consolidate the helper, without changing production code. The consolidated helper preserves generated-hook bytes and verification output.

The Linux transcript includes:

```text
[fixture] Plugin convergence entered; waiting past its 15000ms deadline.
[fixture] Late config write refused by the expired phase authority.
warning:finalize:plugins:deadline: Update finalization timed out in plugins after 15000ms Cancellation settled before recovery.
Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor repair.
exitCode=1 gatewayRestored=true lateWriteRefused=true custodyReleased=true
```

Latest tooling fix: +140/−146 (net −6), with no production changes. Whole PR: production +701/−423 (net +278); tests/proof +861/−86 (net +775); docs +22/−20.

### Latest review disposition

The exact-head ClawSweeper review on `63bc9ba3ac62fb118f19d2496eb02c76ccd078dc` reports no actionable findings. Its remaining data-model compatibility checklist item is satisfied by the published 2026.9.4-driver Linux qualification described above: it exercises legacy failed history, including empty failure reasons, while retaining the existing ledger schema and persistence format. The review itself confirms that this evidence satisfies the earlier compatibility reminder. No additional migration or schema change is needed. No other Rank-up moves remain.

The committed-branch review of record at this head is scoped-clean, with no actionable P0/P1 findings. The native CI watcher confirmed run 35284407181 is GREEN with zero pending checks. The existing synthetic before/after screenshots were inspected again and displayed in the landing chat; both PR attachment URLs resolve to the expected images.
